summary: Two-browser UI call test (A testa / B testb / C testc). CRITICAL: B never renders [data-testid="incoming-call-screen"] when A clicks start-video-call-btn on the A↔B chat, even though B's WebSocket demonstrably receives the `incoming_call` payload. Captured 4 duplicate `{"type":"incoming_call","call_id":...,"call_type":"video","caller_id":...}` frames on B's WS, followed later by `{"type":"call_ended","reason":"cancelled"}` when A cancelled — proof the signalling reaches the browser but the global CallOrchestrator never calls setCall(incoming). Also observed a WebSocket flap storm (3–7 WS reconnect warnings per page) and transient /api 500 errors on both A and B at /chat load, suggesting a React effect dependency churn. Because B never shows the incoming screen, Accept/Daily-join/mic&cam toggle/B-hangs-up/A-peer-left-toast/Decline/Cancel/Busy/Profile-call/Chat-history scenarios cannot be verified end-to-end. A's outgoing side DOES render (in-call-screen + outgoing-ringing-overlay + call-status-text 'Llamando…') and Daily iframe starts loading (postMessage traffic from https://ovcgroup.daily.co observed on A).

minor.issue: 2× '500 ()' resource errors appear in both A and B console around login→/chat navigation; could not identify which endpoints as it was captured as 'Failed to load resource'. Likely contributing to WS token effect churn.

ui_bugs.issue: B does NOT render [data-testid="incoming-call-screen"] when A initiates a call, even though B's WebSocket receives 4 duplicate `incoming_call` payloads for the correct call_id/chat_id. Modal UI never mounts, so B cannot accept/decline from the UI. Likely causes: (a) multiple WS connections flapping (3+ opens, 2+ closes within login→/chat) means the CallOrchestrator socket that *actually gets* the frame has had its onmessage closure invalidated by a re-render / token-effect re-run; (b) React 18 StrictMode double-mount leaves `alive=false` on the surviving socket; (c) the `setCall(prev => prev ? prev : {...})` guard may be hit if an earlier state (e.g. a prior cancelled call) was not fully cleared. Repro: open two browser contexts (viewport 390×844, mic+cam permissions), login A testa@brunoqa.com and B testb@brunoqa.com, both to /chat, A clicks the chat with 'Prueba B' and clicks [data-testid="start-video-call-btn"]; wait 15 s. Expected: B shows incoming-call-screen within ~5 s. Observed: B shows nothing (incoming count = 0 after 15 s) while WS log shows the frame was received.

Four separate components each open their own `new WebSocket(${WS_URL}/api/ws/chat/${token})` connection on authenticated pages. Together with React effect churn, we see 3–7 WS open/close pairs per page per route change, which (1) multiplies server load, (2) delivers every broadcast 4× to the client, and (3) is the suspected root-cause of the incoming-screen miss (handler attached to a socket that is closing). Consolidate into a single shared WS context.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix B not rendering incoming-call-screen. Suspected fixes (in priority order): (1) Deduplicate WebSocket connections — introduce a single shared chat-WS provider (context + hook) used by CallOrchestrator, ChatPage, FloatingChatBubble and RealtimeNotificationContext; this alone will likely resolve the race. (2) In CallOrchestrator useEffect, don't depend on `token` alone — add `user?.id` gating and avoid tearing the socket on StrictMode remount; use a ref to keep the socket across remounts. (3) When processing incoming_call, don't gate on `prev ? prev : {...}` — if prev is stale (e.g. a previous answered call that was supposed to be nulled), log a warning and still replace; or compare by call_id and overwrite when call_id differs. (4) Investigate why 2× /api endpoints return 500 right after login→/chat — the cascading errors may be the trigger for the token effect re-run.
HIGH: Resolve the WebSocket connection flap (3+ opens + closes per account on login→/chat). Add a short debounce or move the connect() into a stable ref.
MED: Investigate the two Failed-to-load-resource 500 errors on both A and B at /chat load.
LOW: `postMessage` origin warnings from Daily iframe (ovcgroup.daily.co) are noisy but non-fatal; Daily SDK itself emits them. Can be ignored.
critical_code_review_comments: CallOrchestrator.jsx opens its own WebSocket, duplicating ChatPage/FloatingChatBubble/RealtimeNotificationContext sockets — 4 connections to the same /api/ws/chat/<token> endpoint from a single tab is wasteful and causes the current bug.

CallOrchestrator.jsx line 78: `setCall((prev) => prev ? prev : {...})` silently drops incoming_call events if any prev state exists. If an earlier call wasn't cleared (e.g. a race on `call_ended` arriving after an `incoming_call` for a different call_id), the new incoming will be ignored. Prefer: `if (prev && prev.id === data.call_id) return prev; return {...new state};`.

WebSocket useEffect in CallOrchestrator depends only on [token]. React 18 StrictMode will double-run the effect in dev; even in prod any transient token change (e.g. during AuthContext hydration) immediately tears and recreates the socket. Add a ref-guard so an already-open socket isn't closed.
chat.id-less path in CallOrchestrator onStart (line 34-38) silently returns if `chatId` can't be resolved from a peer id — add an error toast to aid debugging.

Two separate test invocations also showed 500 response errors on /chat load without further detail — add better error surfacing (brunoToast or at least a console.error) when the chat page fails to load any resource.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The bug is reproducible 100% of the time. Minimal repro: open two Chromium contexts (mic+cam permission grants, viewport 390x844), login A (testa@brunoqa.com) and B (testb@brunoqa.com), both navigate to /chat, A opens the Prueba-B chat, clicks [data-testid=start-video-call-btn]. B's `[data-testid=incoming-call-screen]` never appears within 15 s. However, B's WebSocket DOES receive `{type:'incoming_call', call_id, call_type:'video', caller_id, ...}` 4× (one per duplicated chat WS). Use playwright `page.on('websocket', ...)` + `ws.on('framereceived', payload => ...)` to confirm. A's outgoing side renders [data-testid=in-call-screen], [data-testid=outgoing-ringing-overlay], [data-testid=call-status-text]='Prueba B · Llamando…' correctly. Daily iframe begins loading on A (observed postMessage warnings from https://ovcgroup.daily.co). Fake-media Chromium flags are NOT applied by the browser-automation runner, so Daily video join may still fail even if the incoming-side bug is fixed — mark Daily join as PENDING if that persists.
rca_of_the_issue: Root cause (strong hypothesis — direct patch suggested in action_items #1): CallOrchestrator, ChatPage, FloatingChatBubble and RealtimeNotificationContext each independently open `new WebSocket(/api/ws/chat/<token>)` with useEffect([token]). On login→/chat the token effect runs multiple times (StrictMode + AuthContext hydration), creating/destroying 3–7 WS connections per tab. The backend fan-out broadcasts `incoming_call` to all alive sockets of the recipient — but CallOrchestrator's own socket is often the one being torn down, so its onmessage handler either never fires or fires after `alive=false` was set in cleanup. Reproduction confirms the signal reaches other sockets (we captured 4 copies) while the UI stays empty. Mitigation: consolidate to a single shared WS context + ref-guarded socket in CallOrchestrator, and relax the `prev ? prev : {...}` guard to compare by call_id.
